issues.failure_explanation: For a nonuniform prior, the paper proves only convergence of the marginal mean and variance of each one-step factor $\ell_n$. The interval length is the correlated product $L_n=\prod_{i=1}^n\ell_i$, and the paper itself notes that the factors can be dependent. Convergence of the marginal means does not determine $\mathbb E[L_n]$ or its exponential rate, so the advertised arbitrary-prior expected convergence rate is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: We compute expected convergence rates with respect to any arbitrary a priori distribution for the position of the root in the initial interval and proved that it depends only on the the expectation $\mathbb{E}[c(1-c)]$ of the cut $c$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must control the joint law of the factors and derive the asymptotics of $\mathbb E[\prod_{i=1}^n\ell_i]$, or weaken the scope claim to convergence of one-step marginal moments.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's advertised extension of its expected interval-length rate from a uniform prior to every prior is not justified; only an asymptotic one-step contraction statistic is obtained.
issues.title: Arbitrary-prior expected convergence rate is not established
issues.why_classification: Preserving the arbitrary-prior expected convergence-rate guarantee requires a new argument about correlated products; otherwise a central advertised guarantee must be withdrawn.

issues.failure_explanation: If $f(c_n)=0$, the algorithm does not terminate but enters the else branch and sets $a_{n+1}=c_n=r$. At the next iteration, $f(a_{n+1})=0$, so the strict test again fails; a later cut to the right of $r$ replaces the lower endpoint and excludes the root, violating the stated invariant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit $f(c_n)=0$ termination case, or otherwise preserve a zero endpoint rather than treating it through the strict-sign else branch.
issues.overall_effect: The returned interval is not guaranteed to contain the root, including for the classical midpoint method when the midpoint happens to be the root.
issues.title: Bisection loses the bracket when a cut is exactly a root
issues.why_classification: A standard local root-detection branch completely restores the bracketing guarantee without changing the method or its rates.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated input permits $r=1$, and the paper permits cut laws with endpoint mass. If $r_n=c_n=1$, the algorithm selects $[1,1]$ and then divides by its zero length. Moreover, at $r=c=0$ the displayed map gives $0/0$ even though the algorithm's strict branch condition behaves differently.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Exclude endpoint roots and zero-length retained intervals, or define explicit absorbing/termination conventions for $r=c=0$ and $r=c=1$ and make the branch conventions consistent.
issues.overall_effect: The rescaled construction and its displayed transition map are not well defined over their full stated domain.
issues.title: The rescaled procedure is undefined at allowed endpoint cases
issues.why_classification: Endpoint conventions or a standard local domain restriction suffice without changing the nondegenerate analysis.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: any real-valued random variable $X$ on $[0,1]$ is characterized by its cumulative distribution function (CDF) $F(x)=\mathbb{P}(X< x)$, which is nonnegative, nondecreasing, right-continuous, and satisfy $F(0)=\mathbb{P}[X=0]$ and $F(1)=1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The function $F(x)=\mathbb P(X<x)$ is generally left-continuous, has $F(0)=0$, and need not have $F(1)=1$ when $X$ has mass at 1. More concretely, if $c=0$ almost surely and $r$ is uniform, then $\ell=1$ almost surely, so the stated strict CDF has $H(1)=0$, while the displayed inclusive Stieltjes formula gives $H(1)=1$. Thus the theorem does not cover the discrete and mixed laws it explicitly promises.

failure_location.quote:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Adopt the standard right-continuous convention $F(x)=\mathbb P(X\le x)$ and consistently replace strict events and integration endpoints throughout, or retain strict CDFs and add the necessary left limits and half-open Stieltjes intervals.
issues.overall_effect: The atom-inclusive distribution formulas and proofs using them are invalid as written, including later factorization and general-root CDF calculations.
issues.title: Strict CDF convention is incompatible with atoms and the Stieltjes formulas
issues.why_classification: The architecture and moment formulas can survive, but a systematic nontrivial repair of all atom and endpoint conventions is required to preserve the advertised arbitrary-distribution scope.

issues.failure_explanation: Independence of $r_n$ from each $\ell_i$ separately does not imply independence of $r_n$ from the vector $(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_n)$. Likewise, independence of the new factor from each previous factor separately does not establish mutual independence, which is what the product expectation in the corollary requires.

failure_location.quote: Assume that $r_n$ is independent from $\ell_i$ ($i=1,\dots,n$). The base case is validated by the computations above. $\ell_{n+1}$ depends only upon $r_n$ and $c_n$ in its construction. $c_n$ is clearly independent from all $\ell_i$. By the induction hypothesis, we can say the same about $r_n$. Thus, $\ell_{n+1}$ is independent from $\ell_1,\dots,\ell_n$ for all $n>0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove by induction the stronger joint factorization that $r_n$ is independent of the full past factor vector and that this vector is mutually independent, using the one-step joint law and independence of each fresh cut.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed factorization $\mathbb E[L_n]=\mathbb E[\ell_1]^n$ lacks a valid proof from the stated induction.
issues.title: Pairwise independence is incorrectly promoted to joint independence
issues.why_classification: A contained but genuinely stronger joint-distribution argument is needed; the existing pairwise argument cannot be repaired by routine algebra.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\mathcal{T}: X \to Y$ be a positive linear operator preserving linear functions.

Therefore, $\mathcal{T}$ preserves all linear functions. As a corollary of \Cref{thm - conv}, we may thus show that under some mild hypothesis, the distributions of the normalized roots $r_n$ always converges uniformly to the uniform distribution

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses allow deterministic midpoint cuts $c_n=1/2$ and an interior point mass $r_0=x$. Then every $r_n$ is a deterministic point $T^n(1/2,x)$, so its CDF remains a step function and cannot converge uniformly to $t$. The invoked operator theorem is also inapplicable: positivity was checked only on nondecreasing CDFs, whereas positivity on $B_\circ[0,1]$ requires $G\ge0\Rightarrow\mathcal TG\ge0$ for arbitrary functions. For $F=\delta_{1/2}$, a nonnegative continuous $G$ peaked at $1/2$ can make $G(t/2)+G((1+t)/2)-G(1/2)<0$.

failure_location.quote:
If $r_0$ does not have a point mass at $0$ or $1$ (that is, $\mathbb{P}[r_0=0]=\mathbb{P}[r_0=1]=0$) and if the cuts $c_n$ are not almost surely at 0 or 1, then 
    \[
    \lim_{k\to\infty} (\mathcal{T}^k G_0)(t) = t \qquad~\textit{uniformly on } [0,1].
    \]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must impose genuinely random/mixing cut hypotheses and supply a valid ergodic or operator argument on an appropriate function or measure space.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed convergence and explicit rate for arbitrary initial laws and admissible cut distributions fail, and the later convergence of factor distributions and moments is not established under those hypotheses.
issues.title: Universal convergence to the uniform root law is false
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false in an important advertised regime, including deterministic classical bisection, and repairing it requires new hypotheses and proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited preceding estimate controls only the supremum distance between CDFs. It does not control the total variation quantity $\int|\mathrm dH_n-\mathrm dH|$; measures can have arbitrarily small Kolmogorov distance while remaining far apart in total variation. The same invalid step is used in the displayed variance estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bypass total variation and apply the integration-by-parts estimates already used in the preceding corollary directly to the supremum bound on $H_n-H$, with adjusted constants.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed derivation of the quantitative mean and variance bounds is invalid as written.
issues.title: Kolmogorov distance is incorrectly used to bound total variation
